clips.environment: Pre-dawn interior of a Macedonian command tent at the Gaugamela camp: lamplight and a brazier, canvas walls, a simple cot. Two armed Macedonian guards stand motionless over the sleeping man. FIRST FRAME already shows this strange image.
clips.scene: LINEAR OPEN, hook front-loaded. Hazel whispers to her own lens while armed guards watch a sleeping man by lamplight; she glances back at the cot mid-line; the last ~3 seconds HOLD on her slow deadpan into the lens, no words.
clips.dialogue: HAZEL (whisper): "Gaugamela. 331 BC. Tonight, an empire two hundred and twenty years old gets a new owner — and the man who's about to take it—" (glance back at the cot) "—is still asleep." Alexander sleeps; he never speaks.
clips.camera: Her handheld selfie lens, arm's length, slight natural sway; the cot with the sleeping king readable behind her over her shoulder. The camera never cuts.
clips.continuity: ALEXANDER asleep per his lock; Hazel scribe wardrobe established here and locked for the episode; guards' Macedonian gear only.
clips.sound: Tent-canvas rustle, distant camp murmur, brazier tick, her whisper.
clips.endingState: Her held deadpan filling frame, eyes to lens; cot and guards unchanged behind her.

clips.environment: Same command tent, minutes later; lamplight, first grey pre-dawn light at the tent flap.
clips.stillComposition: The instant Parmenion bursts in and shakes the waking king awake — Parmenion's hand gripping Alexander's shoulder, mid-shout, weight forward and tense. Alexander is caught mid-rise from the cot, one hand reaching toward his sword belt, face calm despite being startled awake. Hazel stands a few steps back and to the side, near the tent's edge, watching the exchange with alert attention — a genuine bystander physically present in the room, not narrating to any lens, hands empty at her sides. All three figures fully visible together in one wide external frame: Parmenion and Alexander form the foreground focal action; Hazel is a clear, readable secondary figure in the same space; believable eyelines and blocking; real depth and separation between the three bodies and the tent behind them. CAMERA: a real external observer's framing, eye-level, positioned inside the tent at a natural viewing distance, capturing all three figures together in one frame — no camera, phone, or rig in anyone's hand, no POV distortion, no fisheye, no arm's-length selfie perspective.
clips.scene: Parmenion strides in visibly rattled and shakes the sleeping king awake. Alexander wakes instantly calm, already reaching for his sword belt, unhurried. Mid-scene a wax tablet is pressed into Hazel's hands without explanation; she fumbles the stylus (running-gag plant).
clips.timeline: 0-2s: Parmenion enters, shakes him, speaks. 2-5s: Alexander wakes calm, reaches for sword belt, Parmenion presses his question. 5-8s: Alexander answers while buckling armor, half-amused; the tablet is pressed into Hazel's hands. 8-9s: her fumbled-stylus line.
clips.dialogue: PACING IS EXPLICIT PER CHARACTER AND MUST BE FOLLOWED EXACTLY — do not apply one uniform tempo across this exchange; the contrast between Parmenion's urgency and Alexander's unhurried calm IS the scene's performance point, sustained the whole 9 seconds, not just on isolated lines. PARMENION (fast, clipped, breathless with urgency, shaking him): "My lord. MY LORD." — the second "MY LORD" louder and sharper than the first, no space between his two lines. PARMENION (still fast, words tumbling just behind his own movement, worked up): "You could have taken them in the dark last night. Why do you STILL refuse a night attack?" ALEXANDER (EXTREMELY SLOW, unhurried, deliberate, weighty — even while his hands move quickly buckling armor, his VOICE is markedly slower than Parmenion's, with genuine two-second silences between each sentence, never rushed through — match @Audio2's tempo exactly, including its long pauses): "I will not steal a victory, Parmenion." (long two-second pause, no dialogue, just his calm breathing and hands working) "Let it be daylight," (brief pause) "and let it be earned." (another long pause) ALEXANDER (to Hazel, still slow and unhurried, half-amused, not rushed, looking directly at her as he speaks — match @Audio2's tempo): "You write quickly?" HAZEL (HER EYES ARE THE MOST IMPORTANT DETAIL OF THIS BEAT: the instant Alexander's voice turns to address her, her eyes lift OFF THE TABLET and lock onto his face — this eye contact is held, unbroken, for the rest of the shot; she does NOT look back down at the tablet, the stylus, her hands, or anywhere else while she is speaking — a full beat of hesitation before she speaks at all — thrown by the tablet suddenly in her hands, not composed yet; then a dry, slightly startled-amused delivery, unhurried, not swept into the room's urgency, fumbling the stylus by feel without looking at it, her gaze staying on Alexander's face the entire time she talks): "...Apparently—" (small pause) "—as of right now, yes." Only after her line fully ends and a beat passes does she finally look back down at the tablet.
clips.camera: A real external observer's frame inside the tent, all three visible together; the camera holds a natural viewing distance and reframes only to keep the group readable as they move — Parmenion looming over the cot, Alexander rising into it, the tablet pressed into Hazel's hands. EYELINES ARE THE MOST CRITICAL BLOCKING DETAIL IN THIS SHOT AND MUST BE FOLLOWED EXACTLY: when Alexander speaks directly to Hazel ("You write quickly?"), his eyes are on her face, not on the middle distance or on Parmenion. Hazel's eyes are on the tablet ONLY during the brief silent writing beat before Alexander speaks to her — the MOMENT his voice turns toward her, her eyes come UP and lock onto his face, and stay locked on his face through her entire spoken answer; she is never looking down at the tablet, at her hands, off to the side, or at nothing while she is speaking or while he is speaking to her. This is a face-to-face exchange between two people who are looking at each other, not a woman absorbed in writing while a man talks near her. No POV, no selfie framing, nobody's eyeline is the lens. The camera never cuts.
clips.continuity: Both NPC locks verbatim; the wax diptych tablet and stylus debut here and are tracked for the rest of the episode. Alexander's unhurried pacing here is the same locked trait as every other clip (§32) — this scene does not suspend it, it is the scene that proves it.
clips.sound: Parmenion's footsteps and breath urgent, close, and quick; Alexander's own movements steadier and unhurried under his armor's small-sounds even as his hands work fast; canvas.
clips.endingState: Tablet in her hands, stylus recovered awkwardly; Alexander mid-arming; Parmenion still tense.

clips.environment: Same tent; a worn leather scroll-case lies by the cot (worn, plain — never an ornate fantasy prop).
clips.stillComposition: The opening instant of the scene, continuing directly from clip 2: Hazel's own handheld selfie framing, arm's length, viewer's eyes as the lens. Alexander is mid-arming in frame — buckling a strap, his attention on his own gear, not looking at her. A worn, plain leather scroll-case is visible by the cot, in her eyeline, the thing she has just noticed and is about to ask about. No phone, camera, rig, or mount visible. Selfie POV, natural handheld framing, Alexander readable at arm's-length distance from her.
clips.scene: Arming continues through the WHOLE beat — he buckles, checks the blade, moves; the scene must never read as two people pausing to chat. She nods at the scroll-case; his answers land mid-motion; he is OUT of the tent on his last word — the scene exits into momentum.
clips.timeline: 0-2s: she nods at the scroll-case, asks (Hazel, 3 words, unhurried). 2-11s: he answers without looking up, still arming (Alexander, 15 words @ ~130 wpm, near-natural pace with emphasis, not a slow read). 11-14s: her line (Hazel, 7 words, unhurried, dry). 14-25s: his final line landing mid-stride as he snaps the last buckle and exits on the last word (Alexander, 19 words @ ~130 wpm, voice stays measured and economical through the exit motion, with one deliberate beat of contrast right before the final word).
clips.dialogue: PACING PER CHARACTER (corrected per short-form retention rule — near-natural rate, NOT sub-natural): Hazel's is easy, curious, unhurried — a genuine question, not rushed, ~140 wpm. Alexander's VOICE conveys unhurried/economical through EMPHASIS and PAUSE PLACEMENT, not through an overall slow rate — his actual word rate stays near-natural (~130 wpm); the 'unhurried' quality comes from a single deliberate beat of contrast right before his last word, not from a uniformly slow read, even as his HANDS and BODY move fast arming; his vocal pace and his physical pace are deliberately independent of each other, but his voice must never drag or sound sedated. HAZEL (easy, curious, mild wonder, unhurried, natural conversational pace; her eyes on him, watching him arm himself): "What's that?" ALEXANDER (EYES DOWN, fixed on his own hands and the strap/blade he is working — NEVER lifting toward Hazel or the lens during this entire line, not even briefly; voice measured and economical at a near-natural pace, weight carried by emphasis on "Aristotle's," "corrected," and "dagger," not by slowness): "Homer. Aristotle's own copy — he corrected it himself. Sleeps under my pillow. With the dagger." HAZEL (dry, a small amused edge at the image of a scholar-warrior sleeping with a book and a knife, still unhurried, natural pace; eyes still on him): "You brought a book to a war." ALEXANDER (snapping the last buckle, already moving past her; his voice STAYS measured and economical through this line at a near-natural pace even though his body is now in full motion toward the exit — one deliberate beat of contrast right before the final word "too," not a slow read throughout; EYES DOWN/AHEAD on his own path exactly like the first line for all but the very last word — ONLY on that last word do his eyes lift and land on her, one brief glance, before he is gone from frame): "I brought the only book that matters. Achilles didn't get old either. I intend to beat that record too."
clips.camera: Her handheld selfie lens tracking his motion past her; she turns to follow his exit. EYELINES (restated, do not deviate): Alexander's eyes point DOWN at his own hands/gear through his entire first line — zero glances at Hazel or the lens during that line. Through his second line his eyes stay down/ahead on his own path for the whole line except the single final word, where they lift and land on her for one brief beat, then he exits frame — this is the ONLY moment he looks at her in the whole clip. Hazel's eyes are on him for the entire beat, unbroken — watching him arm himself, then turning to track his exit as he passes her; she never looks away from him. If in doubt, default Alexander's gaze DOWN, not up. The camera never cuts.
clips.continuity: ALEXANDER lock; motion never stops; scroll-case worn leather.
clips.sound: Armor small-sounds, canvas, distant horses waking.
clips.endingState: Tent flap swinging from his exit; she is turning to follow.

clips.environment: Walking through the waking Macedonian camp to the horse lines at first light; in the distance the Persian campfires stretch to the horizon with no visible end. A separately-guarded plain tent with two armed guards, NO royal iconography.
clips.scene: Walk-and-talk to the horse lines: the horizon of Persian fires behind her; Bucephalus pins his ears at everyone but Alexander (who is nearby at the lines); passing the guarded tent she drops her voice for the captives fact.
clips.timeline: 0-5s: walking, the fires line the horizon behind her, first line (12 words @ ~145 wpm). 5-10s: at the horse lines — Bucephalus, ears pinned, calms only toward Alexander; her Bucephalus line (11 words @ ~145 wpm). 10-17s: passing the separately-guarded tent, quieter, the captives line (13 words @ ~125 wpm, slower delivery).
clips.dialogue: HAZEL: "Darius pulled soldiers from more than twenty different peoples for this. Twenty." HAZEL: "This is Bucephalus. Only he's ever been allowed to ride him." HAZEL (quieter, passing the guarded tent): "That one — Darius's own mother and wife. Captured two years ago. Still here."
clips.camera: Her handheld selfie lens, walking; deep frame carries the endless fires, then the horse lines, then the guarded tent. The camera never cuts.
clips.continuity: BUCEPHALUS lock debuts exactly as written; Persian fires innumerable, no visible end; guarded tent plain.
clips.sound: Camp waking — hooves shifting, leather, low voices, fires; her voice close.
clips.endingState: She is past the guarded tent, glancing back at it; horse lines behind.

The episode's ONE sweeping camera move: travelling alongside the Companion cavalry wedge as it assembles and drives left-to-right, Alexander at its point on Bucephalus, the torn gap in the Persian line deep frame-right. No dialogue — horns and massed hooves only.
clips.camera: The single sweeping lateral travel of the episode: camera moves parallel with the wedge, keeping Alexander's point in the right third of frame, the gap deep frame-right growing nearer. One move only; no zoom, no cut.
clips.continuity: ALEXANDER + BUCEPHALUS locks; Macedonian bronze/crimson only on the wedge; Persian side distinct; screen direction LEFT-to-RIGHT absolute; §22 written trace filed with the prompt.
clips.sound: Horns, then massed hooves building. Close: leather, breath; middle: massed hooves, shouted commands; far: continuous unbroken roar. This bed continues unbroken into 5b/6/7.
clips.endingState: Wedge at full gallop, point aimed at the gap deep frame-right; dust building behind.
clips.constraints: Hazel does not appear. No faces of hers anywhere.

clips.inheritedState: The air is ALREADY heavy with dust from the fighting before this shot begins — this is NOT a clean battlefield; visibility at distance is already reduced.
clips.scene: THE IMPACT. The Macedonian cavalry wedge (bronze helmets, crimson cloaks, leveled lances, entering from frame-left) charges the remaining distance left-to-right and SLAMS into the massed Persian infantry line right-of-center. At the point of contact the Persian formation visibly BUCKLES — wicker shields dropping, spears turning away, men scattering sideways out of the wedge's path — and the break propagates outward from that single contact point while the Persian line further from the breach still holds intact. Cause and effect in one sustained frame. At the contact point: dropped shields, snapped spears, men and horses falling (visible and real, never graphic or gory), riderless horses breaking loose.
clips.camera: The camera never moves. Completely static locked camera, no zoom, no pan, no cut, no change of framing at any point during the entire 6 seconds; compressed flattened telephoto perspective stacking the colliding masses.
clips.continuity: The two armies' equipment NEVER mixes: bronze-and-crimson cavalry from the left, varied Persian contingents with wicker shields, turbans, patterned fabrics on the right. Screen direction LEFT-to-RIGHT.
clips.sound: Hoofbeats accelerating, then the impact itself — a timber-and-metal mass collision landing over the roar. Close: leather, breath, individual cries; middle: massed hooves, shouted commands; far: continuous unbroken roar.
clips.endingState: The breach torn open right-of-center, break still spreading outward; the far line still holding; dust thickened over the contact point.

clips.scene: DARIUS FLEES — opens ON her face: scleral show, mouth dropping to a full O, hands rising then clamping the tablet, shoulders pulling in. She half-turns; deep in frame a distinct chariot-and-standard wheels hard and recedes AWAY (deeper-right); nearby Persians glance toward it, one beat, then break and run — the collapse streaming past her on both sides, wounded among them, equipment underfoot. NOTE: this clip carries the episode's ONE subjective-sound beat (a ~2s muffle at the realization) — implemented at the EDIT stage, not in generation audio.

clips.dialogue: HAZEL (breathless): "...That's him. He's LEAVING. And now everyone else is too."
clips.camera: Her handheld selfie lens: opens tight on her face, widens as she half-turns so the deep frame carries the fleeing chariot and the breaking line; the collapse streams past both edges. The camera never cuts.

clips.endingState: The collapse streaming past her; the chariot a receding speck; her eyes back to the lens.

clips.timeline: 0-1s: beat, she settles to speak. 1-17s: the empire line (36 words @ ~130 wpm — weighty but not yet softened). 17-18s: hold on her steady expression, hard cut to 9b.
clips.dialogue: PACING: weighty, matter-of-fact reveal — not rushed, not urgent; the fact's own gravity carries the pace, target ~130 wpm. HAZEL (steady, direct to lens, matter-of-fact, not yet soft): "Cyrus built that empire two hundred and twenty years ago. It ended today, because a man who overslept his own war refused to win it in the dark — and because one king turned his chariot around."
clips.camera: Her handheld selfie lens, steady; campfires relighting in the deep frame behind her. EYELINE: her eyes stay on the lens/viewer for the entire line — she is not writing here, the tablet is held low and calm, out of her sightline, and her gaze never drops to it. The camera never cuts.

clips.endingState: Hold one beat on her steady expression after the line lands; hard cut to 9b.
